A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EB-1WL/EB-GNN research. All 23 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable; text extraction and visual inspection support matching the methods, proofs, figures and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original EB-GNN experiments on CSL, BREC, QMD, QM9 and MalNet-Tiny, plus measured preprocessing and training times.

after.justification: v2 retains original EB-GNN experiments and reports additional NC-GNN comparisons, alongside the retained runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The core undirected update equations remain unchanged. v2 Appendix B introduces a directed MalNet-Tiny adaptation: embeddings exist only for present edge directions, incidence aggregations use directed neighborhoods, and triangle aggregation substitutes the reverse orientation when necessary. This adds a procedural variant without redesigning the core architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CSL, BREC, QMD, QM9 and MalNet-Tiny tasks. Appendix D examines a pair already belonging to BREC; it does not add dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds NC-GNN to the synthetic, QMD and MalNet-Tiny comparisons. Its expressivity table also adds I2-GNN, DRFWL and 4-ℓ-GIN, substantially expanding comparator membership beyond v1's MPNN, triangle-augmented MPNN and 2WL. The QM9 comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve their metrics, epoch and batch-size budgets, embedding sizes, hyperparameter grids and validation-based selection procedures. New NC-GNN comparisons reuse the stated training or tuning procedures. The added directed implementation description does not establish a separate revision to the retained evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a focused BREC graph-pair case study and verification code concerning triangle information on both nodes and edges. This extends v1's aggregate comparison against node triangle-count features. Existing synthetic analyses and QM9 timing measurements remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations, with ten seeds for QMD/QM9 and five for MalNet-Tiny. Additional baseline rows follow the existing reporting practice; the revised MalNet-Tiny mean and deviation do not establish a change in statistical methodology.

E6.justification: New comparator results substantially extend the empirical findings: NC-GNN distinguishes zero BREC Extension pairs versus EB-GNN's 60, and EB-GNN has lower MAE on six of eight QMD tasks. MalNet-Tiny EB-GNN accuracy changes from 93.22 ± 0.41 to 93.30 ± 0.66; this is a revised report, not an established same-setting improvement. Existing EB-GNN molecular and synthetic scores and measured runtimes are retained.

T1.justification: v2 adds conditional triangle-enumeration optimality and arboricity arguments, a formal comparison with δ-k-LWL, and a claimed separation from 1WL supplied with node and edge triangle counts. The principal expressivity theorems remain; v1's Proposition 2 and Theorem 1 are combined rather than replaced by new results. v1's homomorphism Example 2 and its dimension-one network remark are removed.

C1.justification: The central expressivity, efficiency and general-purpose performance claims remain. v2 adds the explicit abstract-level claim that EB-GNN has the strongest known theoretical expressivity guarantees among edge-based message-passing GNNs, strengthening its novelty positioning without replacing the main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new NC-GNN comparisons as empirical support for the theoretical expressivity advantage. Appendices A and C add substantive explanations of triangle-based message passing, graph-family scalability and differences from local WL updates. The dense-graph, node-task and link-prediction limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds details of hash-map triangle enumeration, directed MalNet-Tiny processing and graph-pair verification code. The implementation link changes from GitHub to an anonymous 4open.science repository. Hardware, training settings and hyperparameter grids are otherwise retained in the experimental appendix, relocated from A to B.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands positioning against edge-based chemical models and efficient higher-order methods, including δ-k-LWL, SetWL and PPGN. New citations support these comparisons and the complexity discussion. References concerning low-dimensional expressivity are removed along with the corresponding remark.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around two research questions and an explicit contributions narrative. Related work is reorganized, the NC-1WL comparison becomes a unified two-part theorem, and proof presentation is revised. The appendix organization expands from the experimental appendix to Appendices A–D.

P2.justification: v2 enlarges and color-codes Figure 2, separates previously adjacent figures and tables, and reorganizes the empirical displays. The expressivity table gains a runtime column and comparator rows. New Figures 4 and 5 display the BREC graph pair and verification code.

improvement.justification: Direct NC-GNN comparisons address a relevant empirical omission in v1, while clearer implementation explanations improve assessability. These support a limited overall gain, despite defects in the new theoretical examples: Appendix C's worked path update conflicts with its stated rule, and Figure 5 sums endpoint triangle counts rather than counting triangles containing each edge, leaving Appendix D's stronger separation claim unsupported by that check.
